segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Hello. Jonathan Briggs, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: JB
segments.en: Yes, that’s right.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: DO come in and sit down.

segments.speaker: JB
segments.en: Thanks.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Right. Well, Jonathan, as we explained in your letter, in this part of the interview we like to talk through your application form .. . your experience to date, etc. .. . and then in the second part you go for a group interview.

segments.speaker: JB
segments.en: Group interview . .. yes, I understand ...

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: So ... your first degree was in Economics?

segments.speaker: JB
segments.en: Yes, but I also did Politics as a major strand.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: And you graduated in 1989. And I see you have been doing some teaching . ..

segments.speaker: JB
segments.en: Yes. I worked as a volunteer teacher in West Africa. I was there for almost three years in total from 1990 to ... umm ... 1992.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: How interesting. What organisation was that with?

segments.speaker: JB
segments.en: It’s not one of the major ones. It’s called Teach South.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Oh, right. Yes, I have heard of it. It operates in several African countries, doesn’t it? And what kind of school was it?

segments.speaker: JB
segments.en: A rural co-operative.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Oh, a rural co-operative, how interesting ... and what did you teach?

segments.speaker: JB
segments.en: A variety of things in different years ... ummm ... I did ... with Forms 1 to 3 mainly Geography and some English with Form 5. Then in my final year I took on some Agricultural Science with the top year . .. that’s Form 6.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Right. Quite a variety then . ..

segments.speaker: JB
segments.en: I also ran the school farm.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: ... And how did you find the whole experience? Tipescripts

segments.speaker: JB
segments.en: I’ll be honest with you. At the end of the first year I really wanted to leave and come home.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Why was that?

segments.speaker: JB
segments.en: Well. .. I was very homesick at first and missed my family ...

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Umm ... I can quite understand that.

segments.speaker: JB
segments.en: ... and I also found it frustrating to have so few teaching resources, but I did decide to stay and in the end I extended my tour to a third year.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Right. Things must have looked up then?

segments.speaker: JB
segments.en: Yes. We set up a very successful project breeding cattle to sell locally.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Really?

segments.speaker: JB
segments.en: And then after a lot of hard work we finally got funds for new farm buildings.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: And you wanted to see things through?

segments.speaker: JB
segments.en: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: And is that why you want to train to teach Geography?

segments.speaker: JB
segments.en: Yes. I’ve had a couple of jobs since then but I now realise I like teaching best. And I chose Geography because . .. because it is my favourite subject... and also because I think it has so many useful applications.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Well. .. you certainly have had some interesting work experience. I’ll ask you now to go on to the next stage of ...
